title: run_governor_cycle is not hermetic: cycle tests read and write the machine's real ~/.needle state
description:
run_governor_cycle reads live host state unconditionally, so every mock_poller_tests cycle test depends on (and mutates) the developer's real governor data:

- Step 5a calls calibrator::read_all_scores() -> ~/.needle/state/prediction-accuracy.jsonl (calibrator.rs:292 default_accuracy_path).
- Step 2 calls collector::run_collection_pass() and reads collector::default_db_path().

Neither has a path-injection or env-override hook; there is no seam for tests.

Observed damage: test_cycle_holds_emergency_brake_safe_mode_at_98_percent passed early in a session and failed later on the same commit. The host file had grown to 99 scores with |median error| 1.31 (< SAFE_MODE_EXIT_ERROR_THRESHOLD 8.0), so update_safe_mode_from_calibration took the exit branch and wiped the seeded emergency_brake safe_mode before the assertion. Some of those 99 scores were appended by the test run itself.

Worked around in bf-rkrd5 by pinning safe_mode.scored_at_entry = u32::MAX in seed_braked_state, which holds predictions_since_entry at 0 for any ambient score count. That covers those two tests only; every other cycle test is still exposed.

Fix: thread the accuracy path and collector DB path through run_governor_cycle (or a config/env override) so tests can point them at a TempDir.

agents:
  # claude-print workers (Anthropic subscription billing, cc_entrypoint=cli)
  # Requires: claude-print installed (needle run --agent claude-anthropic-sonnet)
  # Session pattern: NEEDLE names sessions as needle-claude-anthropic-sonnet-<workspace>-<N>
  claude-print-sonnet:
    launch_cmd: needle run --agent claude-anthropic-sonnet --workspace {workspace}
    session_pattern: needle-claude-anthropic-sonnet-*
    heartbeat_dir: ~/.needle/state/heartbeats
    min_workers: 0
    max_workers: 8
    subscription: true   # marks workers as subscription-billed (see entrypoint filtering)

OBSERVED session naming from tmux: 'needle-claude-anthropic-sonnet-vcd-1' confirms pattern needle-claude-anthropic-sonnet-*.

This template should be wired to whatever subscription flag is added to AgentConfig (separate bead).

title: Fix cgov --version: hardcoded 0.1.0 out of sync with Cargo.toml 0.1.1

Fix:

2. Add a unit test in src/main.rs asserting the clap Cli version equals env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION") so the two can never drift again.
3. Also check install.sh and README.md for hardcoded version strings (none found in static review, but verify).

Acceptance criteria:

title: Surface alert_fp_telemetry re-enablement progress in cgov doctor / a new cgov alerts view
description: governor.yaml's alerts.auto_bead comment states the re-enablement criterion: 'Re-enable only after FP rate < 5% over 100-alert window.' The AlertFpTelemetry struct in src/state.rs already tracks recorded sample count, false-positive count, and aggregate FP rate per alert type, and cgov status --json already emits it as the alert_fp_telemetry field, but there is no human-facing view of progress toward the 100-sample threshold - an operator has to know to grep the JSON. Add a doctor check in src/doctor.rs, or a small new cgov alerts subcommand, that reports per alert type: samples recorded so far, current FP rate, and how many more samples are needed before the 100-sample / 5-percent-FP re-enablement bar is met, so there is a visible trackable path back to auto_bead true instead of the setting being indefinitely stuck at false with no visible momentum. Note this telemetry currently only accumulates while the governor daemon (the hidden _daemon subcommand) is actually running and evaluating alert conditions each cycle, so this is most useful once the daemon is confirmed running again (see the separate bead about the currently stopped daemon, bf-hjage) and complements the stateful alert dedup bead bf-5k6yv and ADR-001 in docs/plan/plan.md.

GAP: docs/plan/plan.md contains ADR-001 (2026-07-20, status Proposed) — "Split the governor daemon into an always-on Observe loop and a separately-gated Act loop." The decision is documented in detail but NOT implemented, and no bead tracked it. The ADR's own Follow-up section says the concrete extraction steps "should be filed as their own beads once someone picks this ADR up." The smaller sibling problems from that same investigation are already tracked (bf-5l61f duplicate systemd units in_progress, bf-47asm br->bf alert cmd, bf-3vjam pricing models, bf-5k6yv alert dedup, bf-2fqc9 fp telemetry surfacing, bf-hjage document disabled daemon), but the core split itself had none.

EVIDENCE (absent in artifacts):
- src/main.rs exposes only Daemon / _Daemon subcommands (hidden `_daemon`); there are no `_observe` / `_act` subcommands. run_internal_daemon_command just calls run_daemon_command (one coupled loop).
- src/governor.rs run_daemon bundles observe (poll -> burn-rate EMA -> capacity forecast -> confidence cone -> calibrator -> safe-mode) with act (apply_scaling worker launch/SIGINT) and alert (check_alerts / fire_alert) behind one on/off switch.
- config/ still ships coupled unit(s); no claude-governor-observe.service / claude-governor-act.service exist.

WHY IT MATTERS (ADR Context): because observe+act+alert are one process, the only way to stop acting on distrusted predictions is to kill the whole daemon, which also stops the harmless read-only Observe half — starving the calibrator and FP-telemetry of the data needed to decide when it is safe to re-enable acting (self-perpetuating blackout; ex44 daemon was stale 21+ days, see bf-hjage).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- ADR-001 status advanced Proposed -> Accepted (or close wontfix if rejected) BEFORE implementation — respect the ADR's "once someone picks this ADR up" gate.
- `cgov _observe` (hidden): poll -> EMA -> capacity forecast -> confidence cone -> calibrator -> safe-mode every loop_interval; writes governor-state.json / governor-state.prev.json / prediction-accuracy.jsonl; NEVER runs launch_cmd, never SIGINT/kills a worker, never runs the alert command.
- `cgov _act` (hidden): reads state _observe wrote; performs only apply_scaling() and check_alerts()/fire_alert().
- governor-state.json ownership split enforced: _observe owns usage/capacity_forecast/burn_rate/schedule/calibration/safe_mode/alert_fp_telemetry; _act owns workers.*.target/alert_cooldown and appends alerts (no torn-write race).
- Two systemd units (claude-governor-observe.service enabled+Restart=always by default; claude-governor-act.service independently stop/disable-able), coordinated with bf-5l61f. cgov enable installs+starts both; cgov stop/disable gain target arg (observe|act|all, default all) so `cgov stop act` = pause acting, keep observing.
- cgov doctor checks _observe and _act independently: stopped _observe = fail; deliberately-stopped _act = warn, not fail.
- Tests: _observe performs no worker/alert side effects; _act no-ops on fresh-unchanged state; doctor reports the observe/act distinction.

title: Calibration-based safe_mode exit can release an emergency_brake safe_mode while utilization is still >=98%
description:
governor.rs:4573-4577 documents the split: step 1b clears only emergency_brake-triggered safe_mode, and only once max utilization drops below EMERGENCY_BRAKE_THRESHOLD; calibration-triggered safe_mode is left to update_safe_mode_from_calibration.

The reverse direction is not guarded. update_safe_mode_from_calibration (governor.rs:4290) branches on safe_mode.active alone, ignoring safe_mode.trigger, and on exit does *safe_mode = SafeModeState::default() — so good prediction accuracy releases a brake that fired for a capacity emergency, even while utilization is still at 98%+.

Ordering makes it more than cosmetic: step 5a runs at governor.rs:5285, before the effective hysteresis / composite-risk / cone-scaling / target-ceiling overrides are chosen at 5303-5360, which all read state.safe_mode.active. So the cycle that clears it also makes its scaling decision with non-conservative settings. The brake re-arms at 5993 only if the fresh forecast still reaches ScalingDecision::EmergencyBrake and only when !dry_run.

Found while verifying bf-rkrd5. Decide the intended semantics before changing behaviour: most likely the exit branch should skip (or require a separate condition for) trigger == emergency_brake.

title: Implement stale-heartbeat handling per plan: 60s threshold, tmux verification, orphan file removal
description:
Plan section: Component 6 (Worker Manager), 'Heartbeat file format' subsection in docs/plan/plan.md. Spec: 'Heartbeat files older than 60 seconds are treated as stale — the worker may have crashed without cleanup. Stale heartbeats are verified against tmux list-sessions before any action is taken; if the tmux session no longer exists, the heartbeat file is removed.'

Current state (static review): src/worker.rs read_heartbeats() (~line 401) parses all heartbeat JSON files with NO staleness check on the heartbeat timestamp, and nothing anywhere removes orphaned heartbeat files. Consequences:
- After a worker crashes without cleanup, its heartbeat file persists forever; WorkerCount.consistent (count_workers, ~line 118) stays false permanently and heartbeat_count is inflated.
- find_workers_to_stop() (~line 373) can select a dead worker's session (it sorts old heartbeats first as 'may be dead'), causing scale-down cycles to send SIGINT/kill to nonexistent tmux sessions and burn the scale-down budget on ghosts.
Note: the governor already uses tmux_count as the authoritative current count (src/governor.rs ~line 1475), so scaling targets are correct — the gap is stale-file hygiene and shutdown-selection correctness, exactly what the plan specifies.

Implement in src/worker.rs:
1. Add a staleness threshold (60s, ideally a named const) comparing the heartbeat's updated_at/timestamp field to now.
2. When a heartbeat is stale, verify against tmux list-sessions: if the session no longer exists, delete the heartbeat file (log at info level); if the session exists, treat status as executing (never kill based on a stale idle status).
3. Exclude removed/orphaned heartbeats from heartbeat_count and from find_workers_to_stop candidates.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests: (a) stale heartbeat + dead session => file removed and excluded from counts; (b) stale heartbeat + live session => retained but never selected as idle for shutdown; (c) fresh heartbeat behavior unchanged
- count_workers().consistent recovers to true after a crashed worker's heartbeat is cleaned up
- No behavior change for fresh (<60s) heartbeats; cargo test passes

title: Multi-agent scale-down priority: reduce highest-dollar-cost agent first
description:
The plan (§6 Worker Manager / governor.yaml multi-agent orchestration) specifies that when scaling down under cutoff_risk, the governor should reduce the agent with the highest per-worker dollar cost first (Opus before Sonnet before Haiku). The current implementation iterates agents without priority ordering during scale-down decisions.

**Plan reference:** 'When scaling down under cutoff_risk, the governor reduces the agent with the highest per-worker dollar cost first (Opus before Sonnet before Haiku). When scaling up, the governor adds workers to the agent with the lowest per-worker cost that has capacity (current < max_workers).'

**Scope:**
- In governor.rs, when compute_target_workers triggers a scale-down, sort agents by per-worker dollar cost descending before reducing
- When scaling up, sort agents by per-worker dollar cost ascending
- Use burn_rate.by_model dollar rate or agent baseline_burn_rate as the cost proxy
- Add unit test: 2 agents (Opus @ $9/hr, Sonnet @ $5/hr), scale-down — verify Opus reduced first

description:

3. If size >= log_max_bytes: rename governor.log -> governor.log.1, governor.log.1 -> governor.log.2, etc. up to log_backup_count; truncate/create new governor.log

title: Implement governor-side p5h/p7d/p7ds annotation of collector records (unblocks empirical promotion validation)
description:
Plan sections: Component 2 (Token Collector — 'p5h, p7d, p7ds are null at write time. The governor annotates them in the SQLite mirror by apportioning each window's observed percentage delta across concurrent sessions, weighted by total-usd') and Phase 1b step 3 (window_pct_deltas annotation) in docs/plan/plan.md.

Current state (static review): the annotation step was never implemented. src/collector.rs writes p5h/p7d/p7ds as null on both i and f records; a comment in src/governor.rs (~line 1503) confirms: 'The fleet record's p5h/p7d/p7ds fields are always null (the collector writes them null and never fills them in)'. The governor works around this for burn-rate EMA by diffing consecutive API poll snapshots, so scaling works — but downstream features that read the annotated columns are permanently dead:
1. compute_empirical_promo_ratio() in src/burn_rate.rs (~line 498) queries i records WHERE p7ds IS NOT NULL AND p7ds > 0 — always returns no rows, so validate_promotion_from_db() always fails with 'no data found in token-history DB' and empirical promotion validation can never succeed (the conservative 1.0 multiplier fallback would be used through an entire real promotion).
2. The usd-per-pct-7ds column and the promo_check / instance_compare SQLite views in src/db.rs compute NULL forever.

Implement:
1. In the governor cycle (src/governor.rs), after each poll: take the per-window pct delta between consecutive API snapshots for the interval matching the latest collector records, and UPDATE the i rows for that interval in the SQLite mirror (~/.needle/state/token-history.db), apportioning each window's delta across concurrent sessions weighted by each row's total_usd. Fill the f row for the interval with the full (unapportioned) deltas.
2. Guard conditions per plan Component 5: skip when the interval spans a window reset, when elapsed < 2 min, or when worker count changed mid-interval.
3. Keep JSONL authoritative-but-null semantics (annotation lives in the DB mirror, per plan) — do not rewrite JSONL lines.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit test: given 2 synthetic i rows with total_usd 0.10 and 0.30 and a window delta of 0.8, annotation writes p7ds 0.2 and 0.6 respectively; f row gets 0.8
- Unit test: compute_empirical_promo_ratio() returns Some(...) after annotation of >=10 peak and >=10 off-peak synthetic intervals
- instance_compare and promo_check views return non-NULL usd_per_pct_7ds for annotated intervals
- cargo test passes; no changes to scaling behavior when annotation data is absent (existing API-delta EMA path untouched)

1. Scan ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl for files where first user-type line has entrypoint=cli

5. If no agents are configured as subscription: skip check (INFO level)

This check surfaces the case where claude-print is installed but workers are somehow using sdk-cli billing (e.g., claude-print misconfigured, trust dialog stuck, PTY spawn failure).

title: Alert-bead dedup is cooldown-only, not stateful — replace bead-per-firing with one tracked bead per condition episode
description: src/alerts.rs::should_fire()/process_alerts() dedup purely on a per-alert-type cooldown timer (default 60 minutes, alerts.cooldown_minutes in governor.yaml): while a condition remains true past the cooldown window, fire_alert() creates a brand-new bead via the configured command every time the cooldown elapses, rather than tracking one open bead per distinct condition episode. Historical bead data in this repo's own .beads workspace bears this out: bf list --json shows 226 closed beads titled starting with '[WARNING] sonnet_cutoff_risk' and 160 titled '[CRITICAL] cutoff_imminent' (out of 517 total issue_type=human alert beads created historically), almost certainly representing far fewer distinct real incidents than that count of beads. Redesign the alert lifecycle: on first firing of a given (alert_type, window) condition, create one bead and remember its bead id in governor-state.json (e.g. under alert_cooldown or a new open_alert_beads map); on subsequent cycles where the condition is still true, update/comment on the existing bead instead of creating a new one (or simply suppress, since the bead is already open and visible); when the condition clears, auto-close the bead. This is a natural extension of the auto_bead FP-rate gating work already done (see docs-878a, notes/bf-h7toj.md, and the alert_fp_telemetry struct in src/state.rs which already tracks true/false-positive outcomes per alert type) and should be done as part of re-enabling alerts.auto_bead so re-enablement doesn't reproduce the original spam problem. References ADR-001 in docs/plan/plan.md.

title: Consolidate duplicate systemd units cgov.service and claude-governor.service
description: config/cgov.service and config/claude-governor.service both ship as 'the governor daemon' unit for the same logical process, but they differ in ways that matter: claude-governor.service runs 'cgov _daemon' (the hidden systemd-oriented subcommand, Restart=always, Wants=claude-token-collector.service) while cgov.service runs 'cgov daemon' (the public foreground subcommand meant for manual/interactive use, Restart=on-failure, no Wants dependency). An operator who installs/enables cgov.service instead of claude-governor.service gets different restart semantics and no ordering guarantee relative to the token collector, with no clear signal which one is canonical. docs/plan/plan.md's File Layout section documents cgov.service as 'Systemd user service — governor daemon' and claude-governor.service as 'Alternative governor daemon service name', which is itself the source of the ambiguity. Pick one canonical unit name and ExecStart target (claude-governor.service invoking the hidden _daemon subcommand is the correct one, matching Phase 6.2 of the plan), remove or clearly deprecate the other in config/, install.sh, and cgov init/enable, and update the plan's File Layout section to stop presenting them as equally valid alternatives. On this host both units currently exist under ~/.config/systemd/user/ and are both disabled, so this is a good time to also clean up the live install once the fix lands.

title: Verify newer needle release fixes worker stderr span-leak before re-enabling governor
description:
## Context

On 2026-08-05 claude-governor was stopped on lab because the needle workers it
spawns were filling the root filesystem. A single worker's stderr log reached
33.7 GB and was growing at ~159 GB/hr — roughly 50 minutes from a full disk.

Root cause is in needle itself, not the governor: unbounded tracing span nesting
on the bead claim path. Tracked in the NEEDLE repo as **bf-3uj6i**.

The governor's role is that it is the spawner. It created workers `alpha` (08:40)
and `bravo` (09:00) into `cgov-polish-queue`, ~20 minutes apart, and each fresh
worker restarts the leak from zero. Killing a worker only buys ~20 minutes;
stopping the governor is what actually ended the recurrence.

## Current state on lab

- `claude-governor.service` — stopped, but still `enabled`, so it WILL return on
  reboot and resume spawning leaking workers.
- Deployed needle is **0.2.15**, binary `.needle/bin/needle-stable` dated
  2026-07-31. `.local/bin/needle` is a symlink to that same binary.
- The NEEDLE repo main is at **0.2.16** with a `v0.2.16` tag.
- There is **no `v0.2.15` tag** — tags jump v0.2.12 -> v0.2.16 — so the deployed
  binary is an untagged build somewhere in between.
- 200 commits sit between v0.2.12 and HEAD; scanning their subjects for
  trac/span/instrument/claim/retry surfaced only logging-framework work, nothing
  that clearly addresses span-stack nesting. So do NOT assume 0.2.16 fixes it.

## Deliverables

1. Determine whether needle 0.2.16 (or any release newer than the deployed
   0.2.15 build) actually fixes the span leak — read the guard ordering at
   `src/worker/mod.rs` around the `bead.lifecycle` / `bead.claim` entry points
   in that version, don't rely on changelog wording.
2. If fixed: upgrade the pinned `.needle/bin/needle-stable` on lab to that
   release, restart the governor, and confirm worker stderr stays flat over a
   long run.
3. If not fixed: this is blocked on NEEDLE **bf-3uj6i**. Leave the governor
   stopped, and consider `systemctl --user disable claude-governor.service` so a
   reboot cannot silently restart the disk-fill.
4. Secondary hardening (governor-side, independent of the needle fix): the
   governor owns the `2>> ...stderr.log` redirect it attaches to each spawned
   worker, so it is the right place to cap or rotate that file. A worker-side
   logging bug should not be able to fill the host disk.

## Acceptance criteria

- A definitive yes/no on whether a newer needle fixes the leak, with the
  file/line evidence that supports it.
- Governor is either running on a needle version verified not to leak, or
  deliberately left stopped+disabled with this bead recording why.
- Worker stderr growth is bounded, by needle fix or governor-side rotation.

## Related

- NEEDLE bead **bf-3uj6i** — the upstream fix.
- Same incident also required stopping systemd units `needle-worker@lab-roam-1/2/3`
  (separate wedged workers, still `enabled` and will also return on reboot).

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
Deliverable 1 is already answered: no, 0.2.16 does not fix it.

Checked directly rather than via changelog. NEEDLE repo HEAD is version 0.2.16
(Cargo.toml), and the defective guard ordering is still present verbatim at
src/worker/mod.rs:1608:

    self.bead_lifecycle_span = Some(lifecycle_span.entered());

with the matching bead.claim guard at src/worker/mod.rs:1552. So upgrading lab
from 0.2.15 to 0.2.16 would NOT stop the disk-fill.

Corroborating: this server (Hetzner primary) already runs needle 0.2.16, and it
carries the same unfixed code.

Consequence: this bead is now blocked on NEEDLE bf-3uj6i. Remaining work is
governor-side only:

- Decide on 'systemctl --user disable claude-governor.service' on lab so a reboot
  cannot silently restart the disk-fill (currently stopped but still enabled).
- Implement the cap/rotation on the stderr redirect the governor attaches to each
  spawned worker (deliverable 4). This is the durable defense - it holds
  regardless of when needle is fixed.

Note for whoever implements the cap: needle initialises its fmt layer with no
EnvFilter and no max level (src/cli/mod.rs:713), so RUST_LOG is NOT honored and
the spam cannot be suppressed by environment variable. The cap has to be on the
redirect/sink side. Beware naive 'head -c' truncation in the pipeline - it
SIGPIPEs the writer and would kill the worker.

title: [WARNING] sonnet_cutoff_risk: Seven-day Sonnet window at cutoff risk: 37.0% utilized, 83.7h remaining, margin_hrs=82.2h
close_reason:
Fixed false positive sonnet_cutoff_risk alert

The alert was firing even when margin_hrs was positive (safe). This was caused by missing validation of the margin_hrs field in the alert condition.

Per burn_rate.rs formula:
- margin_hrs = predicted_exhaustion_hours - hours_remaining
- Positive margin_hrs = safe (exhaustion after reset)
- Negative margin_hrs = risky (exhaustion before reset)

The fix adds a check for margin_hrs < 0.0 in both sonnet_cutoff_risk and session_cutoff_risk alert functions to prevent false positives from corrupted state or sign convention mismatches between modules.

Fix commit: 26c399d
Regression tests added to prevent recurrence.

## WindowRecord Struct and Forecast Computation

Implement the WindowRecord struct and the forecast computation for all three windows.

### Files to Modify
- `src/collector.rs` — add WindowRecord and forecast logic

### What to Implement
- `pub struct WindowRecord` with all schema fields:
  - `r: String` (always "w"), `ts: DateTime<Utc>`, `win: String` (window name: "five_hour", "seven_day", "seven_day_sonnet")
  - `pk: bool`, `ceil: f64` (target ceiling from config, e.g. 90.0)
  - `snap: f64` (raw platform utilization %), `reset: DateTime<Utc>` (window reset time)
  - `delta: f64` (pct change this interval), `remain: f64` (`ceil - snap`, NOT `100 - snap`)
  - `hrs_left: f64` (hours until reset), `fleet_pct_hr: f64` (fleet burn rate as pct/hr)
  - `exh_hrs: f64` (`remain / fleet_pct_hr`), `cutoff_risk: u8` (1 if `exh_hrs < hrs_left`)
  - `margin_hrs: f64` (`hrs_left - exh_hrs`)
  - `bind: u8` (1 if most constrained), `safe_w: Option<u32>` (only on binding window)
- `pub fn compute_window_forecast(win: &str, snap: f64, ceil: f64, reset: DateTime<Utc>, now: DateTime<Utc>, fleet_pct_hr: f64, pk: bool) -> WindowRecord`:
  - Compute all derived fields: remain, hrs_left, exh_hrs, cutoff_risk, margin_hrs
  - Leave bind=0 and safe_w=None (set by find_binding_window)

### Test Command
```bash
cargo test --lib collector::tests::window_forecast 2>&1; echo "EXIT: $?"
```

### Pass/Fail Criteria
- Unit test: ceil=90, snap=36 -> remain=54 (NOT 64)
- Unit test: hrs_left computed correctly from reset-now
- Unit test: exh_hrs = remain / fleet_pct_hr with known values
- Unit test: cutoff_risk=1 when exh_hrs < hrs_left
- Unit test: cutoff_risk=0 when exh_hrs > hrs_left
- Unit test: margin_hrs = hrs_left - exh_hrs (can be negative)
- Serialization: WindowRecord serializes with correct field names

title: P7: Cross-window capacity optimization
description:
## Task: Cross-Window Capacity Optimization

Optimize worker count across all three windows simultaneously using marginal cost weighting.

### What to Implement
- In `src/burn_rate.rs` (extend):
  - `window_cost(window: &WindowForecast) -> f64`:
    - scarcity = (1.0 / remaining_pct) * hrs_left
    - Short-horizon capacity is cheap; long-horizon is expensive
  - `composite_risk(n_workers, windows, burn_rate) -> f64`:
    - For each window: compute exhaust_hrs at N workers
    - If exhaust_hrs < hrs_left: risk += window_cost * (hrs_left - exhaust_hrs)
    - Sum across all windows
  - `optimal_workers(windows, burn_rate, max_workers, cost_threshold) -> u32`:
    - Max N where composite_risk(N) < cost_threshold
    - cost_threshold=0.0 (default) = never breach any window (equivalent to binding-window)
    - cost_threshold > 0 allows breaching cheap short-horizon windows
  - State schema extension:
    - `cross_window_optimal` field when enabled
    - Falls back to binding-window formula when disabled or in safe mode
  - Configurable via `cross_window.enabled` and `cross_window.cost_threshold`

### Files
- `src/burn_rate.rs` (extend)
- `src/governor.rs` (use composite risk when enabled)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: window_cost — short horizon cheap, long horizon expensive
- Unit test: composite_risk — 5h near-reset with ample 7d allows more workers
- Unit test: cost_threshold=0 behaves identically to binding-window approach
- Unit test: cost_threshold>0 allows more workers when only cheap windows breach
- Unit test: disabled -> falls back to binding-window
- Unit test: safe mode -> falls back to binding-window

### Acceptance Criteria
- Correctly weights window scarcity by remaining time and capacity
- Default behavior (threshold=0) matches existing binding-window logic
- Positive threshold enables intelligent cross-window optimization
- Disabled by config or safe mode falls back to conservative approach

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P3 fleet EMA (docs-5bu) — needs per-window burn rates
- Depends on: P4 target computation (docs-9uz) — replaces binding-window ceiling

## Task: Per-Instance Burn Rate Computation

Compute per-instance dollar_burn and pct_burn from token collector records.

description:
## Binding Window Selection and Safe Worker Count

Implement binding window detection across all three windows and safe worker computation.

### Files to Modify
- `src/collector.rs` — add binding window and safe worker logic

### What to Implement
- `pub fn find_binding_window(forecasts: &mut [WindowRecord])`:
  - Find the window with the smallest (most negative) margin_hrs
  - Set `bind = 1` on that window, `bind = 0` on others
  - Compute and set `safe_w` only on the binding window
- `pub fn compute_safe_workers(remaining_pct: f64, hrs_left: f64, p75_rate_per_worker: f64) -> u32`:
  - `safe_w = floor(remaining_pct / (p75_rate_per_worker * hrs_left))`
  - If p75_rate_per_worker is 0 or hrs_left is 0, return u32::MAX (no constraint)
  - Floor to nearest integer (conservative)
- `pub fn compute_window_forecasts(usage_snapshot: &UsageSnapshot, fleet_rates: &FleetRates, config: &Config) -> Vec<WindowRecord>`:
  - Generate 3 WindowRecords (five_hour, seven_day, seven_day_sonnet)
  - Call find_binding_window on the set
  - Return all 3 records ready for JSONL append

### Test Command
```bash
cargo test --lib collector::tests::binding 2>&1; echo "EXIT: $?"
```

### Pass/Fail Criteria
- Unit test: 5h window with margin_hrs=-2 vs 7d with margin_hrs=5 -> 5h is binding
- Unit test: 7d_sonnet most constrained -> it gets bind=1
- Unit test: safe_w computation — remaining=50, hrs_left=10, p75_rate=1.0 -> safe_w=5

title: P7: System health diagnostic (cgov doctor)
description:
## Task: System Health Diagnostic (cgov doctor)

Validate the entire governor stack in one command with specific remediation steps.

### What to Implement
- New `src/doctor.rs` module:
  - 12 health checks, each returning Pass/Warn/Fail:
    1. OAuth credentials: valid, >1h? <30min? Expired/missing?
    2. API reachability: 200 OK <2s? Slow? Unreachable?
    3. Token collector: running, cursors advancing? Stale >10min? Not running?
    4. Burn rate samples: >=5 per window? 3-4? <3?
    5. Pricing config: all detected models have entries? Unknown model?
    6. Model generation: rates match known generation? Opus at legacy rates?
    7. Promotion dates: active/future? Expires <48h? Expired in config?
    8. SQLite integrity: PRAGMA integrity_check passes?
    9. JSONL/DB sync: row counts within 1%? Diverge? DB missing?
    10. Daemon status: running, last cycle <2x interval? >2x? Not running?
    11. Log file: exists, <100MB? >100MB? Missing?
    12. Prediction accuracy: median error <5%? 5-10%? >10%?
  - Each check has a specific remediation command on failure
  - `cgov doctor` subcommand:
    - Human output: checkmark/warning/cross table
    - `--json`: structured pass/warn/fail per check
  - Exit codes: 0 = all pass (warnings OK), 1 = any fail

### Files
- `src/doctor.rs` (new module)
- `src/main.rs` (add `cgov doctor` subcommand)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: each check condition triggers correct pass/warn/fail
- Unit test: remediation text matches plan for each failure
- Unit test: exit code 0 with all pass + warnings
- Unit test: exit code 1 with any failure
- Unit test: JSON output schema

### Acceptance Criteria
- All 12 checks implemented with correct thresholds
- Specific remediation commands per failure type
- Both human and JSON output
- Exit codes enable automation

description:
## Incremental JSONL Reader with Shrinkage Guard

Implement the incremental line reader that seeks to a byte offset and reads new lines, with shrinkage detection for log-rotated files.

### Files to Modify
- `src/collector.rs` — add incremental reader function

### What to Implement
- `pub fn read_new_lines(path: &Path, cursor: &mut CursorStore) -> Result<Vec<String>>`:
  - Get stored offset via cursor.get_offset(path)
  - Check current file size: if file size < stored offset, log warning `[collector] cursor reset for {path} (file shrunk: {stored} -> {actual} bytes)` and reset offset to 0
  - Seek to byte offset, read all bytes to EOF
  - Split into lines, filter out empty lines
  - Update cursor with new byte offset (end of file)
  - Return the new lines as Vec<String>

### Test Command
```bash
cargo test --lib collector::tests::read_new 2>&1; echo "EXIT: $?"
```

### Pass/Fail Criteria
- Unit test: write 3 lines to temp file, read_new_lines with offset 0 returns all 3 lines
- Unit test: incremental read — write 2 lines, read (get 2), write 2 more, read again (get only new 2), verify cursor offset updated
- Unit test: shrinkage guard — write 100 bytes, set cursor offset to 100, truncate file to 10 bytes, read_new_lines resets offset to 0 and returns all content
- Unit test: empty file returns empty Vec
- Unit test: file with trailing newline doesn't produce empty trailing line
- Shrinkage guard must log the warning message (capture log output or use tracing test subscriber)

title: Add sustained low cache efficiency alert with configurable threshold and window
description:
## Goal
Fire an alert when the fleet's cache-read-to-total-token ratio stays below a configurable threshold for N consecutive polling intervals. This detects workloads that are not benefiting from prompt caching.

## Why
Low cache efficiency means workers are burning more tokens per task than expected. This affects burn rate accuracy and cost. A sustained drop (not just a single spike) indicates a structural issue worth surfacing.

## Implementation
- In alerts.rs: add LowCacheEfficiency alert variant (already has stub per recent commits)
- Track cache_efficiency_ratio per interval in governor state: cache_reads / total_tokens
- If ratio < config.alerts.low_cache_efficiency_threshold (default: 0.3) for >= N consecutive intervals (default: 3): fire alert
- Alert body: current ratio, threshold, consecutive intervals below threshold
- Respect existing per-alert-type cooldown mechanism
- Expose cache_efficiency_ratio in cgov status output
- Add unit tests for threshold boundary, cooldown, recovery

## Config additions (governor.yaml)
alerts:
  low_cache_efficiency_threshold: 0.3
  low_cache_efficiency_consecutive_intervals: 3

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] cache_efficiency_ratio tracked per poll interval
- [ ] Alert fires when ratio sustained below threshold
- [ ] Cooldown respected (no spam)
- [ ] Ratio visible in cgov status --json
- [ ] Unit tests for boundary conditions

description:
## Task: Main Governor Daemon Loop

Implement the core daemon loop that ties together all components into a continuous governor cycle.

### What to Implement
- In `src/governor.rs`:
  - `run_daemon(config: &Config)`: Main loop:
    1. `usage = poll_usage()` — call the poller
    2. `schedule = compute_schedule()` — peak/off-peak, effective hours
    3. `burn_rate = compute_burn_rate()` — read from collector DB, update EMA
    4. `target = compute_target_workers(usage, schedule, burn_rate)` — per-agent targets
    5. `current = count_workers()` — heartbeat + tmux verification
    6. `apply_scaling(current, target)` — scale up/down with hysteresis
    7. `check_alerts(usage, schedule)` — alert conditions
    8. `write_state()` — atomic state file update
    9. `sleep(LOOP_INTERVAL)` — configurable, default 300s
  - Signal handling: SIGINT/SIGTERM -> graceful shutdown (finish current cycle, exit)
  - Error handling: never crash — log errors, continue to next cycle
  - Logging: structured per-cycle summary with window status, worker counts, actions taken
  - `--dry-run` mode: compute and log everything but skip apply_scaling()

### Files
- `src/governor.rs` (extend)
- `src/main.rs` (add `cgov daemon` and `cgov daemon --dry-run` subcommands)

### Testing Requirements
- Integration test: mock all components, verify correct call sequence
- Unit test: error in one component doesn't crash daemon (logs and continues)
- Unit test: dry-run mode logs target but doesn't scale
- Unit test: signal handling triggers clean exit
- Unit test: state file updated after each cycle

### Acceptance Criteria
- Daemon runs continuously until interrupted
- Never crashes on component errors
- dry-run mode fully functional
- Structured logging per cycle
- State file atomically updated each cycle
- Graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P4 worker manager (docs-x8d) — needs scale_up/scale_down
- Depends on: P4 target computation (docs-9uz) — needs compute_target_workers

title: P3: Fleet-level EMA and capacity forecast
description:
## Task: Fleet-Level EMA and Capacity Forecast

Aggregate instance burn rates into fleet statistics and maintain per-(model, window) EMA for capacity forecasting.

### What to Implement
- In `src/burn_rate.rs`:
  - `FleetBurnStats` struct: mean, p75, stddev of per-worker rates
  - `aggregate_fleet_burn(instances: &[InstanceBurnRate]) -> FleetBurnStats`:
    - Compute mean, p75, stddev across all active sessions
    - p75 is the conservative rate used for capacity planning
  - `EmaState` struct: per-(model, window) EMA value, sample count
  - `update_ema(state: &mut EmaState, new_value: f64, alpha: f64)`:
    - `ema = alpha * new_value + (1 - alpha) * prev_ema`
    - alpha defaults to 0.2 from config
  - `CapacityForecast` struct per window:
    - `target_ceiling`, `current_utilization`, `remaining_pct` (ceil - used)
    - `hours_remaining`, `fleet_pct_per_hour`
    - `predicted_exhaustion_hours` = remaining_pct / fleet_pct_per_hour
    - `cutoff_risk` = exh_hrs < hrs_left
    - `margin_hrs` = hrs_left - exh_hrs
    - `binding` flag, `safe_worker_count`
  - `compute_capacity_forecast(usage, ema_states, workers, config) -> HashMap<String, CapacityForecast>`
  - `find_binding_window(forecasts) -> String`: argmin(margin_hrs)
  - `compute_safe_workers(remaining_pct, hrs_left, p75_rate) -> u32`: floor(remaining / hrs_left / p75)
  - Separate peak/off-peak tokens_per_pct storage for promotion validation
  - Baseline fallback: use baseline_burn_rate from config until 3 valid samples per window
  - Discard samples > 3σ from current EMA per window

### Files
- `src/burn_rate.rs` (extend)
- `src/state.rs` (extend — write burn_rate and capacity_forecast to state file)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: EMA converges to steady-state value after N samples
- Unit test: fleet aggregate p75 and stddev with 3 synthetic instances
- Unit test: capacity forecast — known inputs produce correct exh_hrs, cutoff_risk, margin_hrs
- Unit test: safe_worker_count computation with floor behavior
- Unit test: binding window is the one with smallest margin_hrs
- Unit test: baseline fallback used when < 3 samples per window
- Unit test: outlier rejection (3σ from EMA)
- Unit test: each window independently transitions from baseline to EMA

### Acceptance Criteria
- Per-(model, window) EMA maintains state across cycles
- Capacity forecast computed for all 3 windows
- Binding window correctly identified
- Conservative p75 used for safe_worker_count
- Baseline fallback per-window (not global)
- Outliers rejected without corrupting EMA

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P3 per-instance burn rate (docs-1e4)
- Depends on: P2 schedule calculator (docs-6dm) — needs peak/off-peak classification

close_reason: Fixed: collector now writes heartbeat fleet record when idle to prevent false collector_offline alerts

comments.author: coding
comments.text:
Wrote a zero-usage heartbeat fleet record in run_collection_pass() when session_usage is empty (no new data). Previously the early return skipped the database write, letting the governor's freshness check see a stale t1 timestamp and fire false collector_offline alerts during idle periods.

## Retrospective
- **What worked:** Reading the systemd journal to pinpoint the exact 6-minute gap (10:03:49–10:09:49) where three consecutive 'no new usage data' passes left the fleet aggregate stale, confirming the diagnosis without guessing.
- **What didn't:** Nothing failed — the fix was straightforward once the idle-period gap was confirmed in the logs.
- **Surprise:** The standalone collector service and the governor's embedded collector both run run_collection_pass() independently, so the same idle gap appears in both service logs. The fix covers both paths since they share the same function.
- **Reusable pattern:** When a daemon has a liveness freshness check downstream, any early-return code path that skips the normal heartbeat write will cause false offline alerts. Always write a heartbeat record on every successful pass, even if there is nothing substantive to report.

Implement core schedule awareness functions in src/schedule.rs.

### What to Implement
- New `src/schedule.rs` module:

Implement the InstanceRecord struct and time-based helpers for peak/off-peak detection.

title: [CRITICAL] emergency_brake_activated: Emergency brake active since 2026-04-23T01:21:03.309820710+00:00
[WARNING] sonnet_cutoff_risk: Seven-day Sonnet window at cutoff risk: 15.0% utilized, 145.2h remaining, margin_hrs=-140.6h
Alert thresholding produces 100% false positives; stop auto-creating beads for unvalidated alerts
description:
## Problem

As of 2026-04-23, every single one of the 50 most recently closed beads in claude-governor is a `docs-*` bead that was auto-created from an alert (`sonnet_cutoff_risk`, `cutoff_imminent`, `emergency_brake_activated`, `collector_offline`) and closed with a commit of the form:

```
Document docs-jnvh as emergency_brake_activated false positive (98% util, -17.2h margin)
Document docs-q4sj as sonnet_cutoff_risk false positive (86% util, -16.2h margin)
Document docs-tggx as cutoff_imminent false positive (99% util, -16.2h margin)
```

**FP rate in the observed window: 50/50 = 100%.** This loop produces ~298 commits/7d — about 25% of total repo-wide commit volume — with zero engineering value.

## Fleet impact

- Workers spend ~25% of capacity round-tripping these alerts (alert fires → `docs-*` bead spawns → worker claims → "document as false positive" commit → close).
- When a worker dies mid-alert-handling, the `docs-*` bead becomes an in_progress zombie. 19 of the 53 total in_progress beads on 2026-04-22 were stuck claude-governor alerts with ages 50h–220h.
- Velocity metrics are inflated: real engineering work is ~127 commits/day vs. a reported ~169. The 500 commits/day target is 25% of the way there, not 34%.

## Suspected root cause

The alert bodies report utilization `81%–99%` alongside margins of `-15.2h` to `-23.2h` (negative). A negative margin at sub-100% util is self-contradictory — either the margin math is wrong or the thresholds are inverted. Whichever it is, the predicate that fires these alerts is broken across every alert type uniformly, not just one.

Starting points for investigation:
- Burn-rate / margin calculation that feeds `sonnet_cutoff_risk`, `cutoff_imminent`, `emergency_brake_activated`.
- The `safe_worker_count` fallback logic (separately tracked in recent `docs-yk3r`, `docs-3gh2`, `docs-khar`, `docs-2dy4` beads — all flagged as bugs, none yet fixed).

## Fix in two parts

**(1) Correct the alert predicates** so the FP rate drops below 5% measured across any 100-bead window.

**(2) Interim mitigation: gate the alert→bead pipeline.** Until (1) lands, stop auto-creating beads for these alert classes. Keep the alert logs for diagnosis; don't burn fleet cycles documenting false positives. Concrete options:
  - Feature flag `governor.alerts.auto_bead = false` (fastest).
  - Require N consecutive cycles in alert state before spawning a bead (smooths out momentary spikes).
  - Suppress spawning when margin and utilization are inconsistent (e.g. negative margin at util < 100%).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] FP rate for `sonnet_cutoff_risk`, `cutoff_imminent`, `emergency_brake_activated`, `collector_offline` measured at <5% over a 100-bead rolling window.
- [ ] Beads are no longer auto-spawned for these alert classes until the FP rate target is met (interim mitigation in place within this bead).
- [ ] Telemetry/dashboard exposes alert FP rate so regressions are visible.
- [ ] New test: negative-margin-at-sub-100%-util alert is suppressed at source (consistency check).
- [ ] Existing zombie `docs-*` beads (ages >6h) are closed out as part of landing this fix.

## Related

- `needle-mv9t` (2026-04-22): cross-workspace mend gap — would clean up zombies produced by this loop, but doesn't address the root cause.
- `docs-yk3r`, `docs-3gh2`, `docs-khar`, `docs-2dy4`: previously-identified governor bugs that likely share upstream causes.
close_reason: Alert FP rate fixed: consistency guard suppresses negative-margin-at-sub-100%-util (hard_limit_remaining_pct > 5%), auto_bead disabled in config, EmergencyBrakeActivated bead creation disabled, AlertFpTelemetry added to governor-state.json. Closed 20 zombie docs-* beads. 439/440 tests pass (1 pre-existing unrelated failure in collector).

title: P4: Target worker computation with hysteresis
description:
## Task: Target Worker Computation with Hysteresis

Implement compute_target_workers() and the hysteresis band that prevents scaling oscillation.

### What to Implement
- In `src/governor.rs` (new module):
  - `compute_target_workers(usage, schedule, burn_rate, config) -> u32`:
    - Compute target_ceiling per window from target_utilization
    - remaining_capacity = max(0, target_ceiling - current_pct)
    - target_rate_per_effective_hour = remaining_capacity / effective_hours_remaining
    - target_rate_per_raw_hour = target_rate_per_effective_hour * current_multiplier
    - target_workers = floor(target_rate / burn_rate_per_worker_per_hour)
    - Clamp to [min_workers, max_workers] per agent
    - Use safe_worker_count[binding_window] as ceiling
  - `should_scale(current: u32, target: u32, hysteresis_band: u32) -> ScaleAction`:
    - If current < target - band: scale up
    - If current > target + band: scale down
    - Else: no action (within dead band)
  - `ScaleAction` enum: ScaleUp(u32), ScaleDown(u32), NoAction
  - Default hysteresis_band = 1 (only act when deviation >= 2 workers)
  - Multi-agent: aggregate burn across all enabled agents; scale down highest-cost agent first

### Files
- `src/governor.rs` (new module, partial — main loop in separate task)
- `src/main.rs` (add `mod governor`)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: target computation with known inputs matches hand calculation
- Unit test: hysteresis — target=3, current=4, band=1 -> no action
- Unit test: hysteresis — target=3, current=5, band=1 -> scale down 2
- Unit test: clamping to min/max workers
- Unit test: binding window ceiling overrides target
- Unit test: multi-agent scale-down prefers highest-cost agent

### Acceptance Criteria
- Correct formula matching plan specification
- Hysteresis prevents oscillation on small deviations
- Binding window safe_worker_count acts as hard ceiling
- Multi-agent cost-based scale-down ordering
- All edge cases (zero remaining, past-ceiling) handled

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P3 fleet EMA (docs-5bu) — needs capacity forecast
- Depends on: P2 schedule calculator (docs-6dm) — needs effective hours

title: [CRITICAL] emergency_brake_activated: Emergency brake active since 2026-04-23T01:21:03.309820710+00:00
description:
## False Positive Analysis

**Alert:** emergency_brake_activated (CRITICAL)
**Activated:** 2026-04-23T01:21:03Z
**Bead:** docs-1w6q

### Evidence of false positive

- seven_day window at 100% utilization, margin_hrs=-7.2h, 7.2h remaining
- seven_day_sonnet window at 86% utilization, 7.2h remaining
- Workers at 0 (emergency brake scaled fleet to 0 on activation)
- No active burn — brake itself prevents any token consumption
- Utilization pinned at 100% because with zero workers, no consumption occurs to change the ratio; the window will reset naturally in ~7.2h

### Root cause

Same as prior false positives (docs-3wbo, docs-j5w0, docs-md2q, docs-unw6): the emergency brake triggers at 98% utilization, kills all workers, and then utilization cannot decrease because there's no consumption to shift the ratio. The alert re-fires every 60 minutes (cooldown) until the seven_day window resets.

### Status

False positive — no action required. The window will reset and the brake will clear automatically.
close_reason: Documented docs-1w6q as emergency_brake_activated false positive. Same continuous brake event since 2026-04-23T01:21:03Z — bead created despite EmergencyBrakeActivated disable (commit 4a2f82c), another in-flight race condition. seven_day at 100% util, seven_day_sonnet at 86%, workers at 0, window resets in ~7.2h. Added to alerts.md and committed as 8458e2c.

title: E2E: Verify all CLI subcommands produce valid output
description:
Verify all CLI subcommands work without panics and produce expected output. Run each subcommand and check for basic correctness.

Steps:
1. cgov version — prints version, component status
2. cgov config — prints active config (verify governor.yaml loads)
3. cgov poll — fetches live usage
4. cgov collect — runs one collection pass
5. cgov status — displays dashboard (may need state file from a daemon run)
6. cgov status --json — valid JSON output
7. cgov status --summary — markdown output for NEEDLE injection
8. cgov forecast — per-window forecast (needs state file)
9. cgov forecast --json — valid JSON
10. cgov workers — worker status (needs state file)
11. cgov workers --json — valid JSON
12. cgov token-history --last 5 — recent window records
13. cgov token-history --fleet -n 3 — fleet records
14. cgov token-history --compare — instance comparison
15. cgov token-history --rebuild-db — rebuild SQLite from JSONL
16. cgov simulate --workers 2 --hours 12 — trajectory projection
17. cgov simulate --workers 2 --hours 12 --json — JSON trajectory
18. cgov explain — recent decisions (may be empty)
19. cgov doctor — health checks
20. cgov scale 2 --dry-run — dry-run scale override
21. cgov logs — tail log (needs log file)
22. cgov init --help — verify subcommand exists

For each: verify exit code 0 (or expected non-zero), no panics, output looks reasonable.
close_reason: E2E verified all 22 CLI subcommands. Fixed compile error in simulator.rs (get_burn_rate -> get_burn_rate_for_window). All commands produce valid output with no panics. Non-zero exit codes are intentional: status exits 2 (high capacity pressure), doctor exits 1 (1 failed check: expired promotion), logs exits 1 (log directory missing). All other commands exit 0.

description:
## Task: Alert Condition Checker and Cooldown Dedup

Implement alert condition evaluation with per-type cooldown deduplication.

### What to Implement
- New `src/alerts.rs` module:
  - `AlertType` enum: CutoffImminent, SonnetCutoffRisk, SessionCutoffRisk, BurnRateSpike, Underutilization, TokenRefreshFailing, EmergencyBrakeActivated, PromotionNotApplying, CollectorOffline
  - `AlertCondition` struct: alert_type, message, severity
  - `check_alert_conditions(state: &GovernorState, config: &Config) -> Vec<AlertCondition>`:
    - CutoffImminent: any window cutoff_risk=1 with margin_hrs < -2
    - SonnetCutoffRisk: seven_day_sonnet.cutoff_risk=1
    - SessionCutoffRisk: five_hour.cutoff_risk=1
    - BurnRateSpike: burn_rate_sample > baseline * 2
    - Underutilization: all windows margin_hrs > hrs_left * 0.5
  - `AlertCooldown` struct: per-type `last_fired` timestamps in state
  - `should_fire(alert_type, last_fired, cooldown_minutes) -> bool`:
    - Suppress if same type fired within cooldown_minutes (default 60)
    - Allow if condition cleared and re-triggered after cooldown
  - `update_cooldown(state: &mut GovernorState, alert_type, now)`

### Files
- `src/alerts.rs` (new module)
- `src/main.rs` (add `mod alerts`)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: each alert condition triggers correctly from synthetic state
- Unit test: cooldown suppresses duplicate within window
- Unit test: cooldown allows re-fire after expiry
- Unit test: cooldown allows re-fire after condition cleared and re-triggered
- Unit test: multiple simultaneous alert conditions

### Acceptance Criteria
- All alert types from plan implemented
- Per-type cooldown prevents spam
- Cooldown timestamps persisted in state file
- Alert messages contain specific window names, percentages, and hours

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P3 state store (docs-thy) — needs GovernorState struct

title: Empirically validate 2x off-peak promotion from observed token consumption ratios
description:
## Goal
Validate the 2x off-peak promotion multiplier by comparing observed peak vs off-peak token-per-percent ratios from token-history data. Fall back to 1x if empirical ratio is not within 10% of declared 2.0.

## Why
The promotion schedule is calendar-based (hardcoded March 2026 dates). If the promotion window shifts, expires, or was misconfigured, the governor would over-estimate capacity during off-peak and under-estimate during peak — leading to cutoffs.

## Implementation
- In collector.rs or burn_rate.rs: group token records by peak/off-peak periods using schedule.rs
- Compute avg tokens-per-percent-usage during each period type
- If off_peak_rate / peak_rate is within [1.8, 2.2], accept promotion as active (ratio ~2.0)
- If ratio < 1.8 or data insufficient: fall back to 1x multiplier (conservative)
- If ratio > 2.5: log anomaly alert (possible miscalibration)
- Expose observed_promo_ratio in governor state and cgov status output
- Add test cases for ratio boundary conditions

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Observed promo ratio computed from token-history DB
- [ ] Scheduler uses empirical ratio when sufficient data exists (>= 10 samples each period)
- [ ] Falls back to 1x when data insufficient or ratio out of range
- [ ] observed_promo_ratio surfaced in cgov status --json
- [ ] Alert fired when ratio anomaly detected (> 2.5 or < 0.8)

title: Composite risk optimization: weight binding window by duration, volatility, and margin
description:
## Goal
Replace the current binding window selection (based solely on margin_hrs) with a composite risk score that weights each window by:
- **Margin** (hours remaining before exhaustion)
- **Duration** (5h window is higher risk than 7d window at same margin%)
- **Volatility** (p25/p50/p75 cone spread — wide cone = uncertain forecast = higher risk)
- **Time-to-reset** (how soon can we recover if we exhaust?)

## Why
The current approach picks the window with the smallest margin_hrs absolute. But a 5-hour window with 1hr margin is far more dangerous than a 7-day window with 6hr margin. Duration and volatility should amplify the risk score.

## Proposed Formula
risk_score = (1.0 - margin_pct) * duration_weight * volatility_factor
- duration_weight: 5h → 3.0, 7d → 1.0, 7d-sonnet → 1.5
- volatility_factor: cone_ratio (p75 - p25) / p50 — wider = higher risk

## Implementation
- Add risk_score computation in burn_rate.rs per-window
- Update binding window selection in governor.rs to use max risk_score
- Surface risk_score in state.rs and status_display.rs
- Add unit tests for composite risk edge cases

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] risk_score computed for each window
- [ ] Binding window selected by max risk_score (not min margin_hrs)
- [ ] risk_score visible in cgov status --json
- [ ] Unit tests pass

title: JSONL file discovery and cursor store
description:
## JSONL File Discovery and Cursor Store

Implement file discovery via glob and the persistent cursor store for incremental reading.

### Files to Modify
- `src/collector.rs` — add functions (module already exists with UsageRecord etc.)
- `Cargo.toml` — add `glob` crate dependency if not present

### What to Implement
- `pub fn discover_jsonl_files(base: &Path) -> Vec<PathBuf>` — walks `base/**/*.jsonl` using glob, returns sorted list of paths
- `pub struct CursorStore { cursors: HashMap<PathBuf, u64> }` with:
  - `pub fn load(path: &Path) -> Result<Self>` — loads `~/.needle/state/collector-cursors.json`, returns empty map if file missing
  - `pub fn save(&self, path: &Path) -> Result<()>` — atomic write: serialize to JSON, write to .tmp file, rename to final path
  - `pub fn get_offset(&self, file: &Path) -> u64` — returns stored offset or 0 for unknown files
  - `pub fn set_offset(&mut self, file: &Path, offset: u64)` — updates offset for file

### Test Command
```bash
cargo test --lib collector::tests::cursor 2>&1; echo "EXIT: $?"
```

### Pass/Fail Criteria
- Unit test: CursorStore round-trip — save to temp file, load back, verify all offsets match
- Unit test: load from nonexistent path returns empty CursorStore (no error)
- Unit test: get_offset for unknown file returns 0
- Unit test: discover_jsonl_files finds .jsonl files in nested directories (create temp dir structure)
- Unit test: discover_jsonl_files ignores non-.jsonl files
- Atomic write: save() writes to .tmp then renames (verify by checking no .tmp file remains)

title: Phase 1b: Token Collector daemon
description:
## Phase 1b: Token Collector (Independent Data Capture)

Build the token collector daemon that tails Claude Code JSONL session files and captures model-specific, token-type-specific consumption data.

### Deliverables
- src/collector.rs module:
  - Walk ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl for unprocessed lines
  - Parse assistant message usage blocks (input, output, cache_read, cache_creation with ephemeral_5m and ephemeral_1h tiers)
  - Extract model from message or infer from session path
  - Accumulate deltas per model per collection interval
  - Compute dollar equivalent using pricing from governor.yaml config
  - Append JSONL records to ~/.needle/state/token-history.jsonl (3 record types: i=instance, f=fleet, w=window)
  - Mirror to token-history.db SQLite for fast queries

- Cursor tracking (collector-cursors.json):
  - Store {filepath: byte_offset} for incremental scanning
  - Shrinkage guard: detect truncated files, reset cursor to 0

- SQLite mirror with tables: i, f, w (wide schemas matching JSONL record types)
  - Views: instance_compare, promo_check

- cgov collect CLI subcommand (standalone, no daemon required)
- cgov collect --daemon mode (continuous loop)
- cgov token-history query subcommands (--last, --compare, --fleet, --rebuild-db)

### Tests
- Dollar computation against known API pricing (each tok_type x model)
- Delta verification (second pass emits zero-n records)
- Multi-model attribution
- Fleet variance stats with synthetic data
- Window binding selection (5h vs 7d constraint)

### References
- Plan: /home/coding/claude-governor/docs/plan/plan.md (Phase 1b, lines 1498-1535)
- Token type pricing table in plan (Component 2)
- Record format examples in plan (i, f, w types)

P7: Forecast confidence cone
description:
## Task: Forecast Confidence Cone

Replace single-point exhaustion predictions with range estimates using per-worker variance.

### What to Implement
- In `src/burn_rate.rs` (extend):
  - Compute per-window exhaustion prediction cone:
    - rate_p25 = ema_rate - 0.675 * stddev (optimistic, 25th percentile)
    - rate_p50 = ema_rate (expected)
    - rate_p75 = ema_rate + 0.675 * stddev (conservative, 75th percentile)
    - exh_hrs_p25 = remaining_pct / (rate_p25 * workers) — best case
    - exh_hrs_p50 = remaining_pct / (rate_p50 * workers) — expected
    - exh_hrs_p75 = remaining_pct / (rate_p75 * workers) — worst case
  - `cone_ratio = exh_hrs_p25 / exh_hrs_p75` (or p75/p25 of rates)
  - Decision logic modulation:
    - Narrow cone (ratio < 1.5): act on p50 (confident)
    - Wide cone (ratio > 2.0): act on p75 (conservative)
    - Between: linear blend between p50 and p75
  - Extend `w` record fields: `exh_hrs_p25`, `exh_hrs_p50`, `exh_hrs_p75`, `cone_ratio`
  - Extend `cgov status` output: `CUTOFF 2.0-3.8h` range instead of single value
  - Extend `cgov simulate` to output three trajectory lines (best/expected/worst)
  - Safe mode interaction: always use p75 regardless of cone width

### Files
- `src/burn_rate.rs` (extend)
- `src/collector.rs` (extend w record)
- `src/cli.rs` (extend status display)
- `src/simulator.rs` (extend with cone)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: cone computation with known stddev
- Unit test: narrow cone -> act on p50
- Unit test: wide cone -> act on p75
- Unit test: linear blend in between
- Unit test: safe mode always uses p75
- Unit test: w record contains cone fields

### Acceptance Criteria
- Three-point prediction per window (p25/p50/p75)
- Decision automatically more conservative when variance high
- Status display shows range instead of point estimate
- Safe mode overrides to always-p75
- cone_ratio drives scaling aggressiveness

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P3 fleet EMA (docs-5bu) — needs stddev data
- Depends on: P7 safe mode (docs-ux4) — interacts with safe mode

description:
## Task: Daemon Management — systemd and tmux Modes

Implement cgov start/stop/restart/enable/disable with dual-mode daemon management.

### What to Implement
- In `src/daemon.rs` (new module):
  - Mode detection: check for systemd user session availability
  - **Mode A: systemd user service** (Linux default):
    - `cgov enable`: install unit files, daemon-reload, enable + start both services
    - `cgov disable`: stop + disable both services
    - `cgov start`: start services (must be enabled first)
    - `cgov stop`: graceful stop (governor finishes current cycle)
    - `cgov restart`: stop + start
    - Unit files: claude-governor.service and claude-token-collector.service
  - **Mode B: tmux sessions** (fallback):
    - `cgov start`: `tmux new-session -d -s "claude-governor" "cgov _daemon"` (and token-collector)
    - `cgov stop`: send SIGTERM to tmux session processes
  - `_daemon` internal subcommand: the actual daemon entrypoint (used by both modes)
  - `_token-collector` internal subcommand: token collector entrypoint
  - Store chosen mode in governor.yaml as `daemon_mode: systemd|tmux`
  - `cgov logs --follow` works with both modes (tails log file directly)

### Files
- `src/daemon.rs` (new module)
- `systemd/claude-governor.service` (template)
- `systemd/claude-token-collector.service` (template)
- `src/main.rs` (add daemon subcommands)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: systemd detection logic
- Unit test: service file installation to correct path (~/.config/systemd/user/)
- Unit test: tmux fallback creates correct sessions
- Unit test: stop waits for current cycle completion

### Acceptance Criteria
- Auto-detects systemd vs tmux
- Services survive reboot when enabled via systemd
- tmux fallback works on systems without systemd
- Graceful stop ensures no mid-cycle interruption
- Logs accessible regardless of daemon mode

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P4 main daemon loop (docs-4f7) — needs _daemon entrypoint

title: P1b: Instance record (i) and fleet record (f) JSONL writer
description:
## Task: Instance (i) and Fleet (f) JSONL Record Writer

Implement the JSONL record generation for instance-level and fleet-level token consumption data.

### What to Implement
- In `src/collector.rs`:
  - `InstanceRecord` struct matching the wide `i` record schema:
    - `r: "i"`, `ts`, `t0`, `t1`, `sess`, `sid`, `model`, `pk` (peak flag), `hr_et`, `dow`
    - Token columns: `input-n`, `input-usd`, `output-n`, `output-usd`, `r-cache-n`, `r-cache-usd`, `w-cache-n`, `w-cache-usd`, `w-cache-1h-n`, `w-cache-1h-usd`, `total-usd`
    - Window pct fields: `p5h`, `p7d`, `p7ds` (null at write time, annotated later by governor)
  - `FleetRecord` struct matching the wide `f` record schema:
    - `r: "f"`, timestamps, `pk`, `hr_et`, `dow`, `workers`
    - Per-model columns: `{model}-{tok_type}-n`, `{model}-{tok_type}-usd` for all configured models
    - Fleet totals: `total-usd`, `p75-usd-hr`, `std-usd-hr`
    - Window snapshots: `p5h`, `p7d`, `p7ds`, `usd-per-pct-7ds`
  - `aggregate_to_fleet(instances: &[InstanceRecord]) -> FleetRecord`: Sum instance records, compute per-worker stats (mean, p75, stddev)
  - `append_jsonl(path: &Path, records: &[serde_json::Value])`: Atomic append to JSONL file
  - Peak/off-peak detection: `is_peak(t: DateTime) -> bool` — peak = 8AM-2PM ET weekdays
  - `hr_et` and `dow` computation from timestamp

### Files
- `src/collector.rs`

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: single instance record serializes correctly to expected JSON shape
- Unit test: fleet record aggregation from 2 instances — verify sums and per-worker stats
- Unit test: p75 and stddev computation with 3+ synthetic instances
- Unit test: peak flag correctly set for various times (weekday 10am=peak, weekday 3pm=off-peak, weekend=off-peak)
- Unit test: JSONL append atomicity (no partial writes)
- Unit test: zero-activity models produce zero-filled columns in fleet record

### Acceptance Criteria
- Records match the exact JSONL schema from the plan (field names, types)
- Fleet record includes all configured models even when inactive (zero-filled)
- Per-worker variance stats computed correctly
- JSONL file grows append-only, one JSON object per line

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P1b dollar computation (docs-o6d) — needs DollarBreakdown
- Depends on: P1b usage block parser (docs-s7l) — needs UsageRecord

title: Model attribution and session ID extraction
description:
## Model Attribution and Session ID Extraction

Implement per-message model detection and session ID extraction from file paths.

### Files to Modify
- `src/collector.rs` — add model extraction and session ID functions

### What to Implement
- `pub fn extract_model(message_json: &serde_json::Value) -> String`:
  - Primary: read `model` field from the message JSON object
  - Fallback: if `model` field is missing/null, return "unknown"
- `pub fn extract_session_id(jsonl_path: &Path) -> String`:
  - Extract session ID from the JSONL file path (typically the filename stem without extension)
  - Example: `/home/user/.claude/projects/foo/abc123.jsonl` -> `abc123`
- `pub fn infer_model_from_path(jsonl_path: &Path) -> Option<String>`:
  - If the path contains model hints (e.g., directory name contains "sonnet" or "opus"), return the inferred model
  - This is a secondary fallback when message-level model field is absent
- Update `parse_usage_block` to use these functions for model and session fields

### Test Command
```bash
cargo test --lib collector::tests::model 2>&1; echo "EXIT: $?"
```

### Pass/Fail Criteria
- Unit test: extract_model with `{"model": "claude-sonnet-4-20250514"}` returns "claude-sonnet-4-20250514"
- Unit test: extract_model with no model field returns "unknown"
- Unit test: extract_session_id from typical path returns filename stem
- Unit test: infer_model_from_path returns None for generic paths
- Unit test: multi-model session — two lines with different model fields produce different UsageRecords with correct model each

  - `compute_dollars(usage: &UsageRecord, pricing: &ModelPricing) -> DollarBreakdown`
  - `DollarBreakdown` struct: `input_usd`, `output_usd`, `cache_read_usd`, `cache_write_5m_usd`, `cache_write_1h_usd`, `total_usd`
  - Formula: `tokens * rate_per_mtok / 1_000_000`
  - Load pricing from `governor.yaml` config file (serde_yaml deserialization)
  - Handle unknown models: log warning, fall back to nearest known model pricing

description:
## Task: Underutilization Sprint Trigger

Implement the underutilization detection that triggers a sprint to use capacity before window reset.

### What to Implement
- In `src/alerts.rs` or `src/governor.rs`:
  - `check_underutilization(state: &GovernorState, config: &Config) -> Option<SprintTrigger>`:
    - Trigger when: < 50% used AND < 2h to reset (configurable thresholds)
    - `underutilization_threshold_pct` from config (default 50)
    - `underutilization_hours_remaining` from config (default 2)
  - When triggered: boost to max_workers for the affected agent
  - Create alert/log entry noting the sprint trigger reason
  - Sprint only if no other window has cutoff_risk (safety check)
  - Sprint ends when window resets or usage exceeds threshold

### Files
- `src/alerts.rs` (extend)
- `src/governor.rs` (integrate sprint trigger into scaling logic)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: 45% used, 1.5h to reset -> sprint triggers
- Unit test: 55% used, 1.5h to reset -> no sprint (above threshold)
- Unit test: 45% used, 3h to reset -> no sprint (too far from reset)
- Unit test: sprint inhibited when other window has cutoff_risk
- Unit test: sprint boosts to max_workers

### Acceptance Criteria
- Sprint triggers only when both conditions met
- Cross-window safety check prevents sprint when other windows at risk
- Configurable thresholds from governor.yaml
- Sprint logged clearly as underutilization recovery

### Dependencies

- Depends on: P4 target computation (docs-9uz) — modifies scaling target

## Phase 3: Adaptive Burn Rate Estimator

Empirically calibrate per-model burn rates (%/hr, tokens/hr, $/hr) using observed consumption data.

### Deliverables
- src/burn_rate.rs module:
  - Read instance (i) records from token-history.db for most recent interval
  - Compute per-instance dollar_burn and pct_burn per window from annotated window_pct_deltas
  - Compute fleet-level per_worker_stats (mean, p75, stddev) across active sessions
  - Maintain per-(model, window) EMA with alpha=0.2
  - Generate capacity_forecast per window: fleet_pct_per_hour, predicted_exhaustion_hours, will_exhaust_before_reset, safe_worker_count
  - Identify binding_window (soonest to exhaust)
  - Separate peak/off-peak tokens_per_pct for promotion validation
  - Guard conditions: skip short intervals, changed worker counts, window resets, zero-delta responses
  - Baseline fallback until 3 valid samples per window

- Updated state schema with burn_rate.by_model, last_fleet_aggregate, capacity_forecast
- Per-window capacity forecast logging

### Prerequisites
- Phase 1b (Token Collector) for consumption data
- Phase 2 (Schedule) for peak/off-peak classification

Replace capacity-governor.sh with the full governor daemon that polls usage, computes burn rates, manages workers, and applies scaling decisions.

### Deliverables
- src/governor.rs main daemon loop: poll -> schedule -> burn_rate -> target -> scale -> alert -> write_state
- compute_target_workers() using corrected formula with effective hours and binding window
- apply_scaling() with hysteresis band (avoid oscillation) and graceful scale-down
- Emergency brake: >=98% on any window -> scale to 0 workers
- src/worker.rs:
  - scale_up(n): execute agent.launch_cmd via shell
  - scale_down_graceful(n): read heartbeat JSONs, find idle workers, SIGINT via tmux, kill after timeout
  - count_workers(): heartbeat files + tmux list-sessions verification
- --dry-run mode: compute and log without modifying workers
- cgov daemon subcommand

### Prerequisites
- Phase 1b (Token Collector), Phase 2 (Schedule), Phase 3 (Burn Rate)

### References
- Plan: /home/coding/claude-governor/docs/plan/plan.md (Phase 4, lines 1608-1639)

P1b: Window forecast record (w) and binding window logic
description:
## Task: Window Forecast Record (w) and Binding Window Logic

Implement window forecast records — the primary output of the measurement pipeline.

### What to Implement
- In `src/collector.rs`:
  - `WindowRecord` struct matching the `w` record schema:
    - `r: "w"`, timestamps, `win` (window name), `pk`
    - `ceil` — target ceiling from config (e.g. 90.0)
    - `snap` — raw platform utilization %
    - `reset` — ISO 8601 reset timestamp
    - `delta` — percentage delta this interval
    - `remain` — `ceil - snap` (headroom to ceiling, NOT to 100%)
    - `hrs_left` — hours until window resets
    - `fleet_pct_hr` — fleet burn rate for this window
    - `exh_hrs` — `remain / fleet_pct_hr`
    - `cutoff_risk` — 1 if `exh_hrs < hrs_left`
    - `margin_hrs` — `hrs_left - exh_hrs`
    - `bind` — 1 if this is the most constrained window
    - `safe_w` — max workers where `exh_hrs >= hrs_left` (only on binding window)
  - `compute_window_forecasts(usage_snapshot, fleet_burn_rates, config) -> Vec<WindowRecord>`: Generate 3 records (five_hour, seven_day, seven_day_sonnet)
  - `find_binding_window(forecasts: &[WindowRecord]) -> &WindowRecord`: Smallest/most negative margin_hrs
  - `compute_safe_workers(remaining_pct, hrs_left, p75_rate_per_worker) -> u32`
  - Write 3 `w` records per collection interval after the `f` record

### Files
- `src/collector.rs`

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: window forecast with known values — verify all computed fields
- Unit test: binding window selection when 5h is more constraining than 7d
- Unit test: binding window selection when 7d_sonnet is binding
- Unit test: safe_worker_count computation — verify floor behavior
- Unit test: cutoff_risk=1 when exh_hrs < hrs_left
- Unit test: cutoff_risk=0 when ample headroom
- Unit test: remain uses ceil not 100% (e.g. ceil=85, snap=36 -> remain=49, not 64)

### Acceptance Criteria
- Three w records per interval (one per window)
- Binding window correctly identified
- safe_w only populated on binding window record
- remain computed against target ceiling, not 100%
- All fields match plan schema exactly

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P1b i/f record writer (docs-lfz) — needs fleet burn rate data

P2: Promotion validation against observed consumption
description:
## Task: Promotion Validation Against Observed Consumption

Validate declared promotion multipliers by comparing peak vs off-peak consumption ratios.

### What to Implement
- In `src/schedule.rs` or `src/burn_rate.rs`:
  - `validate_promotion(db: &Connection, promotion: &Promotion) -> PromotionValidation`
  - `PromotionValidation` struct: `validated: bool`, `observed_ratio: f64`, `expected_ratio: f64`, `peak_samples: usize`, `offpeak_samples: usize`
  - Accumulate >=5 peak-hour samples and >=5 off-peak samples at same worker count
  - Compute `observed_ratio = median(tokens_per_pct_offpeak) / median(tokens_per_pct_peak)`
  - Validation rules:
    - If observed_ratio within 10% of declared multiplier: validated=true
    - If observed_ratio < 1.2: promotion likely not applying, fall back to 1x, log warning
    - If observed_ratio > 2.5: unexpected, log anomaly, use observed ratio
  - Write validation result to state: `burn_rate.promotion_validated`
  - Scheduler reads this flag: if false, use multiplier=1.0 (conservative)
  - Use `promo_check` SQLite view for data source

### Files
- `src/schedule.rs` (extend)
- `src/state.rs` (new or extend — state file read/write for promotion_validated flag)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: valid promotion (ratio 1.9-2.1 for declared 2.0) -> validated=true
- Unit test: invalid promotion (ratio 1.0) -> validated=false, fallback to 1x
- Unit test: anomalous ratio (3.0) -> log anomaly, use observed
- Unit test: insufficient samples (<5 peak or <5 off-peak) -> skip validation, use declared
- Unit test: tolerance boundary (exactly ±10%)

### Acceptance Criteria
- Promotion only trusted after empirical validation with sufficient samples
- Conservative fallback (1x) when validation fails
- Anomalous ratios logged but used (better than declared if significantly different)
- State file updated with validation result
- Guards against premature validation with insufficient data

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P2 schedule calculator (docs-6dm) — needs Promotion struct and peak detection
- Depends on: P1b SQLite mirror (docs-0ts) — needs promo_check view for data

title: P7: Prediction accuracy self-calibration
description:
## Task: Prediction Accuracy Self-Calibration

Track prediction accuracy and auto-tune governor parameters based on historical performance.

### What to Implement
- New `src/calibrator.rs` module:
  - `score_prediction(window, predicted_pct, actual_pct) -> PredictionScore`:
    - `prediction_error = actual_final_pct - predicted_final_pct`
    - Negative = conservative, positive = aggressive
    - `correct`: predicted exhaustion matched actual
  - Append scored predictions to `~/.needle/state/prediction-accuracy.jsonl`
  - Hook into window reset events to trigger scoring
  - `CalibrationState`: predictions_scored, median_error per window, auto-tuned params
  - Auto-tuning rules (activated after >= 10 scored predictions per window):
    - Median error < -5 (conservative): increase burn_rate_alpha +0.02, widen hysteresis +0.5
    - Median error > +5 (aggressive): decrease alpha -0.02, tighten hysteresis -0.5
    - Stddev > 10 (unpredictable): lower target_utilization -0.02
  - Clamp ranges: alpha [0.05, 0.5], hysteresis [0, 3], target_util [0.70, 0.98]
  - Write calibration state to governor-state.json
  - Auto-tuning opt-in via `calibration.auto_calibrate: true` in config

### Files
- `src/calibrator.rs` (new module)
- `src/main.rs` (add `mod calibrator`)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: scoring with known prediction/actual pairs
- Unit test: auto-tuning direction — conservative data increases alpha
- Unit test: auto-tuning direction — aggressive data decreases alpha
- Unit test: clamp enforcement at boundaries
- Unit test: no tuning until 10 predictions scored
- Unit test: JSONL append format

### Acceptance Criteria
- Prediction accuracy tracked per window
- Auto-tuning adjusts parameters in correct direction
- Clamps prevent runaway parameter drift
- Opt-in via config (tracking always active, tuning optional)
- JSONL file serves as audit trail

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P3 fleet EMA (docs-5bu) — needs capacity forecast to score
- Depends on: P3 state store (docs-thy) — writes calibration state

description:
## Task: Usage Block Parser and Model Attribution

Parse Claude Code JSONL assistant message usage blocks and extract per-model token counts by type.

### What to Implement
- In `src/collector.rs`, implement:
  - `parse_usage_block(line: &str) -> Option<UsageRecord>`: Parse a JSONL line containing an assistant message with usage data
  - `UsageRecord` struct with fields: `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_5m_tokens`, `cache_write_1h_tokens`, `model: String`, `session: String`
  - Handle nested `usage.cache_creation` sub-object:
    - `usage.cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens` -> cache_write_5m
    - `usage.cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens` -> cache_write_1h
    - Fallback: if sub-object absent, attribute all `cache_creation_input_tokens` to 5m tier
  - Model extraction: read `model` field from message; fallback to inferring from session path
  - Session ID extraction from JSONL file path

### Files
- `src/collector.rs`

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: parse standard usage block with all token types
- Unit test: parse usage block without cache_creation sub-object (fallback to 5m)
- Unit test: parse usage block with zero cache writes
- Unit test: model extraction from message field
- Unit test: model inference from session path when message field absent
- Unit test: multi-model session (different model fields in same file)

### Acceptance Criteria
- Correctly parses all five token types from usage blocks
- Handles missing/partial cache_creation sub-object gracefully
- Model attribution works per-message, not per-session
- Returns None for non-usage lines (tool calls, user messages, etc.)

title: Wire pre-scaling logic for peak/off-peak transitions

Implement the file discovery and incremental scanning subsystem of the Token Collector.
