title: P7: Cache efficiency monitoring
description:
## Task: Cache Efficiency Monitoring

Track per-worker and per-workspace cache hit ratios to identify inefficient consumption.

### What to Implement
- In `src/collector.rs` (extend):
  - Compute `cache_eff` per instance interval: `cache_read_tokens / (cache_read_tokens + input_tokens)`
  - When both are zero: cache_eff = null (undefined, excluded from aggregation)
  - Add `cache_eff` field to `i` records
  - Add `fleet_cache_eff` (mean) and `cache_eff_p25` (25th percentile) to `f` records
- In `src/db.rs` (extend):
  - `workspace_cache_eff` view: per-session average, min, sample count over last 24h
- In `src/alerts.rs` (extend):
  - Cache efficiency warning: when worker drops below `cache_efficiency.warn_threshold` (default 0.60)
    for `consecutive_intervals` (default 3) consecutive intervals
  - Log: `[governor] CACHE: {session} efficiency {eff} (fleet avg {fleet_avg})`
- In `src/cli.rs` (extend cgov status):
  - Add cache efficiency to status output: `Burn: $2.15/hr (p75) · Cache: 84% (fleet avg)`

### Files
- `src/collector.rs` (extend i and f record generation)
- `src/db.rs` (extend with view)
- `src/alerts.rs` (extend with cache alert)
- `src/cli.rs` (extend status display)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: cache_eff computation with known token counts
- Unit test: null cache_eff when both zero
- Unit test: fleet_cache_eff aggregation
- Unit test: warning triggers after 3 consecutive low-efficiency intervals
- Unit test: warning does NOT trigger for transient dips (1-2 intervals)
- Unit test: workspace_cache_eff view returns correct aggregation

### Acceptance Criteria
- Per-instance cache efficiency tracked and stored
- Fleet-level aggregation in f records
- Sustained low efficiency generates warning
- Status display includes cache efficiency metric
- Null handling prevents division by zero

title: P7: Safe mode — automatic conservatism on prediction degradation
description:
## Task: Safe Mode — Automatic Conservatism

When prediction accuracy degrades, enter a conservative fallback mode.

### What to Implement
- In `src/governor.rs` (extend):
  - `check_safe_mode(calibration: &CalibrationState, config: &SafeModeConfig) -> SafeModeState`
  - Entry conditions (OR):
    - Median prediction error > enter_median_error (default 10.0%)
    - Prediction error stddev > enter_stddev (default 15.0%)
  - Effects while active:
    - target_utilization reduced by util_reduction (default 0.10) — e.g. 0.90 -> 0.80
    - hysteresis_band widened by hysteresis_boost (default 1)
    - Sprint disabled
    - Cross-window optimization disabled (fall back to binding-window)
    - Always use p75 (worst-case) from confidence cone
  - Exit conditions (ALL must be true):
    - Median error < exit_median_error (default 7.0%)
    - Stddev < exit_stddev (default 12.0%)
    - At least 3 new predictions scored since entry
  - Hysteresis between entry/exit thresholds prevents toggling
  - State: safe_mode.active, entered_at, trigger, median_error_at_entry, predictions_since_entry
  - Status: `Workers: 2 active (target: 2 · safe ceiling: 2) WARNING SAFE MODE`
  - Manual override: `cgov scale N` overrides for one cycle but safe mode reasserts next cycle

### Files
- `src/governor.rs` (extend)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: safe mode entry on high median error
- Unit test: safe mode entry on high stddev
- Unit test: safe mode exit requires all three conditions
- Unit test: predictions_since_entry counts window reset events

description:
## Task: Promotion Boundary Pre-Scaling

Anticipate multiplier transitions and begin scaling down before the boundary hits.

### What to Implement
- In `src/schedule.rs` (extend):
  - `next_transition(promotions) -> Option<(DateTime, f64, f64)>`:
    - Return next upcoming multiplier change (time, old_multiplier, new_multiplier)
    - E.g., (2026-03-19T08:00:00 ET, 2.0, 1.0) when off-peak ends
  - Pre-scale logic in `src/governor.rs`:
    - If transition within `pre_scale_minutes` (default 30 from config):
      - Compute post-transition target workers using new multiplier
      - If post-transition target < current workers: begin scaling down
      - Scale down at most 1 worker per cycle (gradual)
      - `effective_target = max(post_target, current_workers - 1)`
  - Conservative-only: pre-scale DOWN before losing bonus, never pre-scale UP
  - Logging: `[governor] PRE-SCALE: off-peak→peak in {min}min — scaling {from}→{to} (post-transition safe: {safe})`

### Files
- `src/schedule.rs` (extend with next_transition)
- `src/governor.rs` (extend with pre-scale check)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: next_transition at 07:35 ET during promo returns (08:00, 2.0, 1.0)
- Unit test: next_transition at 13:35 ET during promo returns (14:00, 1.0, 2.0)
- Unit test: pre-scale triggers 30 min before transition
- Unit test: pre-scale does NOT trigger 31 min before transition
- Unit test: pre-scale only scales down, never up
- Unit test: gradual scale-down (max 1 worker per cycle)

### Acceptance Criteria
- Correctly identifies next multiplier transition
- Pre-scales only when losing capacity bonus (conservative-only)
- Gradual scale-down prevents sudden worker drops
- Configurable look-ahead window
- Clear logging of pre-scale decisions

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P2 schedule calculator (docs-6dm)
- Depends on: P4 target computation (docs-9uz)

title: P7: Trajectory simulator (cgov simulate)
description:
## Task: Trajectory Simulator (cgov simulate)

Project future capacity utilization under configurable worker scenarios.

### What to Implement
- New `src/simulator.rs` module:
  - `simulate(config: SimConfig) -> Trajectory`:
    - Walk forward from `now` in 1-minute steps
    - Apply current per-model EMA burn rate from governor-state.json
    - Apply promotion multiplier transitions from promotions.json
    - Handle window resets (utilization drops to 0 when resets_at crossed)
    - Apply configured target_utilization ceilings
  - `SimConfig`: workers (fixed or schedule like "4:6h,2:6h"), hours, resolution
  - `Trajectory`: array of data points at configurable resolution (default 15 min)
  - Each point: timestamp, per-window utilization, promo multiplier, workers, events
  - Detect first ceiling breach per window
  - `cgov simulate` subcommand:
    - `--workers N|SCHEDULE`, `--hours H`, `--json`
    - Human output: ASCII table with window columns and events
    - JSON output: array of trajectory points + breach object
  - Read-only — reads state but makes no changes

### Files
- `src/simulator.rs` (new module)
- `src/main.rs` (add `cgov simulate` subcommand)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: 24h simulation with known burn rate, verify final utilization
- Unit test: window reset mid-simulation (utilization drops to 0)
- Unit test: promotion transition mid-simulation (2x -> 1x at 08:00 ET)
- Unit test: ceiling breach detection at correct time
- Unit test: variable worker schedule ("4:6h,2:6h")
- Unit test: JSON output schema

### Acceptance Criteria
- Accurate projection accounting for promotions, resets, and ceilings
- Variable worker schedules supported
- First breach time identified per window
- Both human and JSON output modes
- Read-only — no side effects

### Dependencies

- Depends on: P2 schedule calculator (docs-6dm) — needs promotion transitions

title: P4: Worker manager — scale up, scale down, count
description:
## Task: Worker Manager — Scale Up, Scale Down, Count

Implement worker lifecycle management via tmux and heartbeat files.

### What to Implement
- New `src/worker.rs` module:
  - `scale_up(agent: &AgentConfig, count: usize)`:
    - Execute `agent.launch_cmd` via `sh -c` for each new worker
    - Stagger launches with 1s delay between each
    - launch_cmd returns immediately (tmux session created in background)
  - `scale_down_graceful(agent: &AgentConfig, count: usize)`:
    - Read heartbeat JSON files from `agent.heartbeat_dir` matching `agent.session_pattern`
    - Find idle workers (status == "idle")
    - Skip attached sessions (check `tmux display-message -t SESSION '#{session_attached}'`)
    - Send SIGINT via `tmux send-keys SESSION C-c`; sleep 2s; then `tmux kill-session`
    - Kill most-recently-launched idle workers first
    - Stop after killing `count` workers or exhausting idle pool
  - `count_workers(agent: &AgentConfig) -> WorkerCount`:
    - Read heartbeat files + verify against `tmux list-sessions`
    - `WorkerCount`: active, idle, executing, stale
    - Stale heartbeats (>60s old): verify against tmux; remove if session gone
  - `Heartbeat` struct: session, agent, status (idle/executing/starting), bead_id, workspace, updated_at, launched_at
  - `read_heartbeat(path: &Path) -> Option<Heartbeat>`
  - **Key principle**: never kill an executing worker. Only idle workers.

### Files
- `src/worker.rs` (new module)
- `src/main.rs` (add `mod worker`)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: heartbeat parsing (all status values)
- Unit test: stale heartbeat detection (>60s old)
- Unit test: idle worker selection (skip executing, skip attached)
- Unit test: kill order (most recent first)
- Integration test: scale_up executes launch_cmd correctly
- Unit test: count_workers correctly categorizes by status

### Acceptance Criteria
- Never kills executing workers
- Never kills attached sessions (human watching)
- Graceful shutdown with SIGINT before kill
- Stale heartbeat cleanup with tmux verification
- launch_cmd executed via shell (supports complex commands)

### Dependencies
- None (standalone module, uses configured agent settings)

description:
## Phase 2: Schedule and Promotion Calculator

Implement off-peak awareness and promotion-period handling so the governor can accurately compute effective remaining capacity.

### Deliverables
- src/schedule.rs module:
  - is_peak_now() -> bool (peak = 8AM-2PM ET weekdays)
  - current_multiplier() -> f64 (1.0 or 2.0 during active promotion)
  - effective_hours_remaining(reset_time) -> f64 (accounts for peak/off-peak segments between now and reset)
  - Reads promotion definitions from promotions.json

- config/promotions.json with current promotion entry

- Promotion validation against measured consumption:
  - Accumulate >=5 peak and >=5 off-peak samples at same worker count
  - Compute observed_ratio = median(tokens_per_pct_offpeak) / median(tokens_per_pct_peak)
  - Validate within 10% of declared multiplier
  - Fall back to 1x if validation fails
  - Write validation result to burn_rate.promotion_validated in state

### Tests
- Peak hour boundary cases (7:59 AM -> off-peak, 8:00 AM -> peak, 2:01 PM -> off-peak)
- Weekend classification (always off-peak)
- Past-promo-end returns 1x
- Effective hours calculation: 40h reset with 30h off-peak should be > 40

### Prerequisites
- Phase 1b (Token Collector) provides the consumption data needed for promotion validation

### References
- Plan: /home/coding/claude-governor/docs/plan/plan.md (Phase 2, lines 1539-1573)

description:
## Task: Token Collector Offline Graceful Degradation

Implement three-tier fallback when the token collector is not running or data is stale.

### What to Implement
- In `src/burn_rate.rs`:
  - `collector_data_age(db: &Connection) -> Duration`: Time since most recent record in token-history.db
  - Three-tier fallback logic:
    - < 10 minutes: use normally (collector may be between cycles)
    - 10-30 minutes: use last EMA values; log `[governor] WARN: collector data stale ({age}s)`
    - > 30 minutes: fall back to `baseline_burn_rate` from governor.yaml; create HUMAN alert bead
  - In fallback mode: dollar-equivalent metrics unavailable; continue with pct-based rates only
  - When collector resumes: return to EMA-based rates within one interval

### Files
- `src/burn_rate.rs` (extend)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: fresh data (< 10 min) -> normal operation
- Unit test: stale data (15 min) -> warning logged, last EMA used
- Unit test: very stale data (45 min) -> baseline fallback, alert created
- Unit test: recovery — after stale period, fresh data restores normal operation

### Acceptance Criteria
- Governor never crashes when collector offline
- Graceful degradation through three tiers
- Alert created at 30-minute threshold (once, with cooldown)
- Recovery to EMA-based rates is automatic

### Dependencies
- Depends on: P3 fleet EMA (docs-5bu) — needs EMA infrastructure

title: P7: End-of-window capacity sprint
description:
## Task: End-of-Window Capacity Sprint

Capture throughput from capacity that would expire unused at window reset.

### What to Implement
- In `src/governor.rs` (extend):
  - `sprint_eligible(window, state, config) -> bool`:
    - Window resets in <= sprint.horizon_minutes (default 90)
    - Remaining headroom > sprint.min_headroom_pct (default 15%)
    - Bead backlog exists (workers have work to do)
    - No other window has cutoff_risk
    - Confidence cone not too wide (cone_ratio <= 2.0)
    - Safe mode NOT active
  - When eligible:
    - Temporarily raise max_workers by sprint.max_workers_boost (default 3)
    - effective_max capped at min(safe_worker_count) across non-sprinting windows
    - Set state: sprint_active, sprint_window, sprint_expires_at
  - Sprint ends when: window resets, headroom < 5%, or safe mode activates
  - Status output: `Workers: 5 active (target: 5 · normal max: 3 · SPRINT on five_hour, resets in 0h42m)`

### Files
- `src/governor.rs` (extend)

### Testing Requirements
- Unit test: sprint triggers with eligible conditions
- Unit test: sprint blocked when other window has cutoff_risk
- Unit test: sprint blocked when headroom too low
- Unit test: sprint blocked when too far from reset
- Unit test: sprint blocked in safe mode
- Unit test: sprint respects cross-window safe_worker_count cap
- Unit test: sprint ends at window reset

### Acceptance Criteria
- Sprint only when conditions safe
- Cross-window safety enforced
- Temporary max_workers boost, reverts automatically
- Sprint state visible in cgov status
- Guards against all inhibiting conditions (safe mode, confidence cone, cross-window risk)

title: FleetRecord aggregation and JSONL append
description:
## FleetRecord Aggregation and JSONL Append

Implement the FleetRecord struct, fleet-level aggregation from instance records, and atomic JSONL append.

### Files to Modify
- `src/collector.rs` — add FleetRecord struct, aggregation, and append functions

### What to Implement
- `pub struct FleetRecord` with wide schema:
  - `r: String` (always "f"), timestamps, `pk: bool`, `hr_et: u8`, `dow: u8`, `workers: u32`
  - Per-model columns: HashMap or flattened struct for `{model}-{tok_type}-n` and `{model}-{tok_type}-usd`
  - Fleet totals: `total_usd: f64`, `p75_usd_hr: f64`, `std_usd_hr: f64`
  - Window snapshots: `p5h: Option<f64>`, `p7d: Option<f64>`, `p7ds: Option<f64>`, `usd_per_pct_7ds: Option<f64>`
- `pub fn aggregate_to_fleet(instances: &[InstanceRecord]) -> FleetRecord`:
  - Sum all token counts and USD amounts across instances
  - Compute `workers` as count of unique sessions
  - Compute per-worker stats: mean USD/hr, p75 USD/hr (sort values, pick 75th percentile index), stddev USD/hr
  - Zero-fill model columns for models not seen in this batch
- `pub fn append_jsonl(path: &Path, records: &[serde_json::Value]) -> Result<()>`:
  - Open file in append mode (create if missing)
  - Write each record as a single JSON line followed by newline
  - Flush and sync to ensure durability

### Test Command
```bash
cargo test --lib collector::tests::fleet 2>&1; echo "EXIT: $?"
```

### Pass/Fail Criteria
- Unit test: aggregate 2 InstanceRecords — verify fleet total_usd = sum of instance total_usd
- Unit test: p75 computation with 3+ instances — verify correct 75th percentile selection
- Unit test: stddev computation with known values matches expected result (within f64 epsilon)
- Unit test: zero-activity models produce zero-filled columns
- Unit test: append_jsonl writes valid JSONL (each line is valid JSON, ends with newline)
- Unit test: append_jsonl to existing file appends without overwriting
